chunks.text:
Name: I_SalesOrder
Type: CDS
Module: SD
Clean Core Level: A
Released CDS interface view for sales order header
I_SalesOrder is the released interface view for sales order header data. Replaces direct SELECTs on VBAK. Provides currency-converted amounts, partner roles, and document-flow information through associations. Use this view in any read access to sales order header data.
chunks.title: Released CDS interface view for sales order header

chunks.text:
Name: I_SalesOrderItem
Type: CDS
Module: SD
Clean Core Level: A
Released CDS interface view for sales order items
I_SalesOrderItem is the released interface view for sales order item data. Replaces direct SELECTs on VBAP. Includes schedule lines, ATP confirmation quantities, and pricing associations.
chunks.title: Released CDS interface view for sales order items

Released CDS view for sales order schedule lines

chunks.title: Released CDS view for sales order schedule lines

Released CDS interface view for material master

Released CDS interface view for FI journal entry

chunks.text:
Name: BAPI_SALESORDER_CREATEFROMDAT2
Type: BAPI
Module: SD
Clean Core Level: B
Classic BAPI for sales order creation
BAPI_SALESORDER_CREATEFROMDAT2 is the classic BAPI for creating sales orders. In an S/4HANA Cloud Public-edition context this BAPI is being replaced by the RAP Behavior Definition I_SalesOrderTP and its CREATE EML operation. Use the BAPI only when RAP is unavailable for the target object.
chunks.title: Classic BAPI for sales order creation

chunks.text:
Name: I_SalesOrderTP
Type: BDEF
Module: SD
Clean Core Level: A
Released RAP behavior definition for sales order
I_SalesOrderTP is the released transactional RAP Behavior Definition for sales order header and item. Use EML CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE / READ against this BDEF instead of legacy BAPIs. Commit work via the COMMIT ENTITIES statement.
chunks.title: Released RAP behavior definition for sales order

chunks.text:
Name: BADI_SD_SALES_BASIC
Type: BADI
Module: SD
Clean Core Level: A
Released BAdI for SD sales-order basic processing
BADI_SD_SALES_BASIC is the released enhancement spot for sales-order basic processing. Use this in place of the legacy USEREXIT_SAVE_DOCUMENT_PREPARE in MV45AFZZ. Cloud-ready, upgrade-safe, fully Clean Core Level A.
chunks.title: Released BAdI for SD sales-order basic processing

chunks.text:
Name: ATP_CUST_BADI
Type: BADI
Module: SD
Clean Core Level: A
Released BAdI for ATP customer customizing
ATP_CUST_BADI is the released enhancement spot for ATP (Available-To-Promise) customer customizing. Use this when LLM output references USEREXIT_ATP_QUANTITY — that user exit does not exist; this BAdI is the real extension point.
chunks.title: Released BAdI for ATP customer customizing

chunks.text:
Pattern: LEVEL_A_DEFINITION
Clean Core Level: A
Clean Core Level A — Released SAP APIs
Level A objects are released SAP APIs and extension points: released CDS interface views (I_*), Released RAP Behavior Definitions (BDEFs) consumed via EML, released BAdIs in published enhancement spots, Application Log (SLG1), Application Jobs (APJ), and the Custom Business Object (CBO) framework. Level A is cloud-ready, upgrade-safe, and the primary target for any new development. Use Level A unless no Level A option exists for the requirement.
chunks.title: Clean Core Level A — Released SAP APIs

chunks.text:
Pattern: LEVEL_B_DEFINITION
Clean Core Level: B
Clean Core Level B — Classic stable interfaces
Level B objects are classic stable SAP interfaces that are supported but legacy: BAPIs, classic BAdIs in customer-namespace enhancement spots, customer exits (USEREXIT_* form routines in named includes such as MV45AFZZ), classic Application Log objects. Level B is acceptable only when a Level A alternative is unavailable. Document the reason for choosing Level B over Level A in the design.
chunks.title: Clean Core Level B — Classic stable interfaces

chunks.text:
Pattern: LEVEL_C_DEFINITION
Clean Core Level: C
Clean Core Level C — Discouraged
Level C is direct access to SAP standard objects bypassing released APIs: direct SELECTs on SAP standard tables (VBAK, MARA, KNA1, BKPF, BSEG, etc.), CALL FUNCTION on unreleased function modules, direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on SAP standard tables, custom log tables instead of SLG1. Level C is discouraged and must be refactored to Level A/B during code review.
chunks.title: Clean Core Level C — Discouraged

chunks.text:
Pattern: LEVEL_D_DEFINITION
Clean Core Level: D
Clean Core Level D — Prohibited
Level D is modification of SAP standard code: implicit enhancements (ENHANCEMENT without released spot), core modifications via SE38/SE80, custom Z* tables receiving direct INSERTs that duplicate SAP standard data, hallucinated extension points (e.g. references to USEREXIT_ATP_QUANTITY which does not exist). Level D is prohibited and blocks the pipeline.
chunks.title: Clean Core Level D — Prohibited

chunks.text:
Pattern: RAP_TRANSACTIONAL
Clean Core Level: A
Use RAP Behavior Definitions for transactional writes
For any transactional operation on a SAP standard business object that has a released RAP Behavior Definition (BDEF), the code MUST use EML (Entity Manipulation Language) against the BDEF rather than calling the classic BAPI. EML CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE / READ on the released BDEF is Level A; the equivalent BAPI is Level B. Commit work via the COMMIT ENTITIES statement.
chunks.title: Use RAP Behavior Definitions for transactional writes

chunks.text:
Pattern: CDS_READ_ACCESS
Clean Core Level: A
Use released CDS interface views for all read access
All read access to SAP standard data MUST go through released CDS interface views (I_*). Direct SELECTs on SAP standard tables are Level C. Released CDS views provide language-dependent texts, currency conversion, authorization, and stable column contracts across SAP releases. Look up the released CDS view in the SAP Business Accelerator Hub before referencing any SAP standard table.
chunks.title: Use released CDS interface views for all read access

metadata.replaces: Direct SELECT on SAP standard tables

chunks.text:
Pattern: EML_WRITES
Clean Core Level: A
Use EML for all writes on RAP-managed objects
Writes to RAP-managed business objects MUST use Entity Manipulation Language (EML): MODIFY ENTITIES OF <BDEF> CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE. Direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the underlying tables is Level C. BAPIs are Level B and acceptable only when no released RAP BDEF exists.
chunks.title: Use EML for all writes on RAP-managed objects

chunks.text:
Pattern: SLG1_LOGGING
Clean Core Level: A
Use Application Log (SLG1) for all logging
All application logging MUST use the SAP Application Log (transaction SLG1) via BAL_LOG_CREATE / BAL_LOG_MSG_ADD / BAL_DB_SAVE or the CL_BALI / CL_BAL_FACTORY class hierarchy. Custom Z log tables are Level C. Register a custom log object and one subobject per business scenario in SLG0 — for example object Z_DARKHORSE with subobjects Z_BACKORDER, Z_RAP, Z_BATCH.
chunks.title: Use Application Log (SLG1) for all logging

chunks.text:
Pattern: APPLICATION_JOBS
Clean Core Level: A
Use Application Jobs (APJ) framework, not classic SM37
Background jobs MUST use the Application Jobs framework: implement IF_APJ_RT_RUN and register a job catalog entry via SE80. Classic SM37 / JOB_OPEN / JOB_CLOSE FMs are Level B. Application Jobs run in S/4HANA Cloud, support job templates, and integrate with the Application Log automatically.
chunks.title: Use Application Jobs (APJ) framework, not classic SM37

chunks.text:
Pattern: BADIS_OVER_USER_EXITS
Clean Core Level: A
Prefer released BAdIs over legacy user exits
When an extension point is needed, use released BAdIs in published enhancement spots (Level A). Legacy customer exits (USEREXIT_* form routines in includes like MV45AFZZ) are Level B and should only be used when no released BAdI covers the requirement. Hallucinated names such as USEREXIT_ATP_QUANTITY do not exist — the corresponding released BAdI is ATP_CUST_BADI.
chunks.title: Prefer released BAdIs over legacy user exits

chunks.text:
Pattern: SIDE_BY_SIDE_EXTENSIBILITY
Clean Core Level: A
Side-by-side extensibility on SAP BTP
New standalone functionality, integrations, and Fiori apps not covered by S/4HANA standard should run side-by-side on SAP BTP — CAP, RAP-on-BTP, Build Apps, Build Process Automation. Side-by-side extensions communicate with S/4HANA exclusively via released APIs (OData, RAP, Events), keeping the digital core clean. This is the preferred extensibility model for greenfield functionality.
chunks.title: Side-by-side extensibility on SAP BTP

chunks.text:
Pattern: IN_APP_EXTENSIBILITY
Clean Core Level: A
In-app extensibility — key user and developer extensions
Small changes within S/4HANA should use in-app extensibility: Key User Extensibility (custom fields, custom logic via cloud-shell IDE BAdIs), Custom Business Objects, Custom Reusable Elements. In-app extensions are persisted as released metadata and survive upgrades. Avoid traditional ABAP development in the digital core except where a released RAP BO and in-app option are unavailable.
chunks.title: In-app extensibility — key user and developer extensions

chunks.text:
Pattern: CBO_CUSTOM_PERSISTENT
Clean Core Level: A
Use the CBO framework for custom persistent data
Custom persistent data MUST use the Custom Business Object (CBO) framework — defined via the Custom Business Object app, exposed as a generated CDS view + RAP BDEF + OData service. Direct creation of Z* tables and writing INSERTs to them is Level C and breaks Cloud compatibility. CBOs participate in the standard transactional lifecycle and authorization model.
chunks.title: Use the CBO framework for custom persistent data

chunks.text:
Pattern: NO_DIRECT_TABLE_INSERTS
Clean Core Level: C
Never write directly to SAP standard tables
Direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on SAP standard tables (VBAK, BKPF, BSEG, KNA1, MARA, etc.) is Level C — and may corrupt downstream SAP processing. All transactional writes MUST go through released RAP BDEFs (Level A) or, when a BDEF is not available, the corresponding BAPI (Level B). The pipeline flags any direct write to a SAP standard table as a Clean Core violation.
chunks.title: Never write directly to SAP standard tables

chunks.text:
Pattern: AGENTIC_AI_AGENTS
Domain: AI
Clean Core Level: A
Agentic AI and AI Agents on SAP BTP
Reference architecture for agentic AI workloads on SAP BTP. Defines the canonical pattern for hosting AI agents that orchestrate SAP processes: agents run on BTP, communicate with S/4HANA exclusively through released APIs (OData, RAP, Events) and BTP Joule services, and never modify the digital core. Use this pattern as the target architecture when DarkHorse or any related agentic system integrates with SAP. Implementation components: SAP AI Core, SAP AI Launchpad, BTP Destinations, BTP Authorization & Trust Management.
chunks.title: Agentic AI and AI Agents on SAP BTP

chunks.text:
Pattern: GENAI_BTP
Domain: AI
Clean Core Level: A
Generative AI on SAP BTP
Reference architecture for generative-AI workloads on SAP BTP. Defines model hosting (SAP AI Core deployments), prompt orchestration via SAP Generative AI Hub, retrieval-augmented generation pattern, and integration with S/4HANA through released APIs. Includes guardrails for data privacy and grounding via Joule and BTP-hosted RAG indexes. Use this pattern when designing any GenAI feature that needs to ground its outputs in SAP data.
chunks.title: Generative AI on SAP BTP

chunks.text:
Pattern: A2A_INTEGRATION
Domain: INTEGRATION
Clean Core Level: A
Application-to-Application Integration on SAP BTP
Reference architecture for synchronous and asynchronous A2A integration. Synchronous: SAP Integration Suite (Cloud Integration / Open Connectors) facing OData / SOAP endpoints. Asynchronous: SAP Event Mesh and event-driven integration with the S/4HANA Event Channel. Avoids direct point-to-point connections and IDoc-only flows where Clean Core APIs exist. Use this pattern for any integration design between SAP and non-SAP applications.
chunks.title: Application-to-Application Integration on SAP BTP

chunks.text:
Pattern: DEVOPS_BTP
Domain: DEVOPS
Clean Core Level: A
DevOps with SAP BTP
Reference architecture for DevOps on SAP BTP. Covers Continuous Integration pipelines for ABAP RAP / CAP / Build Apps via Project Piper, Cloud ALM, SAP Continuous Integration & Delivery service. Defines the canonical pattern for transports, test orchestration, and quality gates. Use this pattern when defining the build and deployment story for DarkHorse-generated code.
chunks.title: DevOps with SAP BTP

chunks.text:
Pattern: NETWEAVER_TRANSITION
Domain: TRANSITION
Clean Core Level: A
Transitioning Architectures from SAP NetWeaver
Reference architecture for moving from SAP NetWeaver-based custom development to Clean Core compliant S/4HANA. Defines the migration path: identify Level C/D modifications, classify against Cloudification Repository, rewrite as side-by-side BTP extensions or in-app extensions, and decommission. Use this pattern as the playbook when DarkHorse must analyze legacy ABAP code for re-platforming.
chunks.title: Transitioning Architectures from SAP NetWeaver

chunks.text:
Pattern: BUILD_PROCESS_AUTOMATION
Domain: AUTOMATION
Clean Core Level: A
Integrate and Extend with SAP Build Process Automation
Reference architecture for low-code process automation on top of SAP using SAP Build Process Automation (BPA). Defines patterns for orchestrating cross-application workflows, automating manual tasks via RPA bots, and exposing automations as triggered services. Always sits side-by-side on BTP — never modifies the digital core. Use this pattern when DarkHorse proposes a process-automation solution rather than custom ABAP.
chunks.title: Integrate and Extend with SAP Build Process Automation

chunks.text:
Pattern: EXTEND_S4HANA_SIDE_BY_SIDE
Domain: EXTENSIBILITY
Clean Core Level: A
Extending S/4HANA with side-by-side apps on BTP
Reference architecture for side-by-side extensions on SAP BTP. Defines how a new app on BTP (CAP, RAP-on-BTP, or Build Apps) consumes S/4HANA released APIs, persists its own data on HANA Cloud, and surfaces in Fiori Launchpad via the Work Zone. The canonical pattern for any net-new functionality where in-app extensibility is insufficient. Use this architecture for greenfield extensions identified during SO/FDS design.
chunks.title: Extending S/4HANA with side-by-side apps on BTP

chunks.text:
Pattern: EVENT_DRIVEN_ARCH
Domain: INTEGRATION
Clean Core Level: A
Event-driven architecture with SAP Event Mesh
Reference architecture for event-driven integration using SAP Event Mesh and the S/4HANA Event Channel. Defines producers (S/4HANA business events, CAP services), brokers (Event Mesh), and consumers (BTP apps, third-party). Use this pattern when a synchronous A2A pattern would introduce tight coupling or blocking — for example, when DarkHorse needs to notify external systems about pipeline-stage completions.
chunks.title: Event-driven architecture with SAP Event Mesh

chunks.text:
Pattern: CAP_ON_BTP
Domain: EXTENSIBILITY
Clean Core Level: A
Building applications with CAP on SAP BTP
Reference architecture for SAP Cloud Application Programming model (CAP) apps deployed on Cloud Foundry or Kyma. Defines CDS-based modeling, service exposure (OData V4), Fiori UI integration, authentication via XSUAA, and consumption of S/4HANA released APIs. The preferred stack for net-new side-by-side apps that need a programming-language choice (Node.js / Java) beyond ABAP.
chunks.title: Building applications with CAP on SAP BTP

chunks.text:
Pattern: RAP_ON_S4HANA
Domain: EXTENSIBILITY
Clean Core Level: A
RAP on S/4HANA — the canonical pattern for in-app transactional development
Reference architecture for ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model on S/4HANA Cloud and Private editions. Defines the layered structure: Data Model (CDS), Behavior Definition (BDEF), Behavior Implementation (BBEH class), Service Definition (SRVD), Service Binding (UI / OData), and EML for all writes. Use this pattern when DarkHorse generates any new transactional object — the TDS object list must contain CDS+BDEF+BBEH+SRVD, not classic PROG/FUGR.
chunks.title: RAP on S/4HANA — the canonical pattern for in-app transactional development
